title: Continental Cup 2026 player-card poster set: grade eight mixed-light pitch-side portraits to one cinematic house look off an in-frame grey card, pop the hero, deepen one kit trim in-family, vectorize the crest, and data-merge one press-ready card per player
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com poster brief for a high-impact football-tournament star poster with cinematic, high-contrast floodlit lighting and print+web delivery. Every real element is laundered: the tournament is the fictional 'Continental Cup 2026', the depicted athletes are eight clearly-fictional players (Diego Solano, Marco Ferraz, Theo Rocher, Luka Petrov, Andre Mensah, Rafael Duarte, Nikolai Ivanic, Samuel Okoye) with no real likeness, and no real club, nation, flag, emblem, competition, sponsor, camera, editing product or social platform is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the literal source brief (drawing/AI-compositing named celebrities and a trophy into one scene) is NOT connector-doable (no text-to-image, no photo compositing, no background-replace-by-prompt, no generative fill). So the client is modeled as a poster/print studio that already photographed its featured players pitch-side and needs the genuine paid craft the brief actually rewards and that 'color_grade_lr' covers: a cross-asset cinematic colour grade that reconciles eight portraits shot under mismatched matchday light to ONE house look (measurable because a photographic 18% grey card was clipped into every frame), a masked hero pop, a masked in-family kit-trim colourway variant without a reshoot, a prep-before-trace vectorisation of the tournament crest, correct triage of a look-alike crest asset that must NOT be traced, and the final card build via a genuine hand-authored single-record page-layout template data-merge into one press-ready ~300 DPI card per player. The eight-portrait count, the mixed matchday lighting, the in-frame grey card, the per-frame casts and the crop dimensions are reasonable enrichment; nothing contradicts the source (star players, cinematic high-contrast grade, print+web delivery are all from the brief).
one_line_ask: Reconcile eight mixed-light pitch-side player portraits to one cinematic Continental Cup house look by neutralising each one to the 18% grey card it carries, pop the hero off the dark stadium, deepen one player's hot collar trim to an in-family colourway without a reshoot, vectorize the tournament crest while correctly triaging a look-alike crest asset away from the tracer, then data-merge the studio's authored card template to produce one press-ready A3 card per player.
full_brief:
We are a poster and print studio producing the official player-card poster set for the Continental Cup 2026, and we need the colour-grade, finishing and final card build. We are NOT reshooting. You are getting eight pitch-side portraits of our featured players, shot across several matchdays under very different light -- some under warm floodlights at night, some in cool twilight, a couple in flat overcast daylight -- and they were not all exposed the same, so straight out of the folder they look like eight unrelated photos, and a poster set that does not read as one campaign looks amateur. To make the match checkable, the photographer clipped a photographic 18% grey card to the pitch-side board in every frame.

The core of the job: bring every portrait to ONE cinematic house look -- a high-contrast, floodlit-at-night feel with deep but never crushed blacks and a warm key -- by neutralising each frame to the grey card it carries so the whole set shares one white point, then carrying each to the same tonal target. Do NOT force one blanket setting across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared look; a set that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will not agree at the grey cards and we will reject it. Keep skin natural and do not blow the floodlit speculars. When you are done, hand back the white-balance and exposure moves you settled on for each frame so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed.

On the featured hero portrait, make the player carve cleanly off the dark stadium -- lift the player, not the whole frame; if the background lifts with him the cinematic depth is gone. One card also needs a colourway variant without a reshoot: that player's collar trim is currently a bright, hot colour and we want a deepened, muted version of the SAME shot in the same colour family for the alternate print run, with the fabric's folds and sheen intact -- just the trim, nothing else in the frame touched. No flat dead-fill, no whole-image tint bleeding onto skin and kit.

We are also sending our tournament crest so it can sit razor-crisp on every card, plus a separate crest asset for a webshop product tile; get each to the right kind of file for its use. Finally, build the set: we have hand-built the card template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (the player photo and the crest); merge our roster into it so every player gets their own press-ready A3 card with their copy bound verbatim, their graded portrait dropped in, and the crest in the masthead, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI PDF covering the whole set, one card per player (the featured hero simply the first card). Bind our copy verbatim -- do not rewrite names, positions or taglines. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the set matched to one house look; the hero carving off the dark background; the trim variant natural under the existing light; a clean vector crest; and exactly one finished card per roster row.

inputs.name: portrait_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched DSLR look, a professional male footballer (fictional, generic face, unbranded plain kit, no logos no flags) standing heroically on a night football pitch under bright stadium floodlights, low-angle hero framing, deliberately FLAT log-style colour (low contrast, milky blacks, slightly warm amber floodlight cast ~3200K), slightly underexposed, real skin pores and hair flyaways, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side advertising board at the far LEFT edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, documentary sports realism, no CGI gloss, no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, whole frame tilted about 4 degrees.
inputs.realism_notes: THE HERO / reference frame that establishes the house look, and it gets the masked subject pop. Deliberately tilted ~4deg (auto-straighten has real work), warm floodlight cast + underexposed (WB + exposure correction real), grey card at FAR LEFT so it neutralises first then crops out when the card frame reframes to the player. ~5200px camera scale (true A3 long edge at 300 DPI is ~4961px, ~5031px including 3mm bleed) so the full-bleed A3 card frame fills at ~300 DPI by downscale only. Its warm floodlight correction is close to portrait_02's but NOT identical, so copying numbers across frames fails.

inputs.name: portrait_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a different fictional male footballer in a plain unbranded kit, arms crossed, on a night football pitch under warm stadium floodlights (~3200K warm amber cast) but exposed a touch BRIGHTER than a typical night frame, flat log-style colour, real fabric and skin texture, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the frame edge, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, level (no tilt).
inputs.realism_notes: Session-A warm frame like the hero but BRIGHTER, so its correction toward the shared target is the warm-to-neutral WB AND a downward exposure nudge, unlike the hero which needs a lift -- two warm frames that still take different corrections. Level, so it must NOT be straightened. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: portrait_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a fictional male footballer in a plain unbranded kit mid-stride, shot at cool blue twilight/dusk before full dark (~5600K cool bluish cast), brighter and flatter than the night frames, real texture, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the edge of frame, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, whole frame tilted about 3 degrees.
inputs.realism_notes: Session-B COOL frame: cooler AND brighter than the hero, so the correct move is the OPPOSITE of the warm frames -- warm the WB toward the target and pull exposure DOWN. Tilted ~3deg (needs straightening, a different angle than the hero). This frame most exposes a naive 'same numbers on all' or per-frame auto-tone approach. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: portrait_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a fictional male footballer in a plain unbranded kit, hands on hips, on a pitch under FLAT overcast daylight (~6000K cool, soft, low-contrast, slightly grey), real texture, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the frame edge, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, level.
inputs.realism_notes: Session-B cool/flat daylight frame: cool cast + flat contrast, needs warming toward the target plus the shared high-contrast tonal build and deep black floor. Level (do not straighten). Another opposite-direction WB from the warm frames. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: portrait_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a fictional male footballer wearing a GENUINELY warm golden-amber training kit (the kit fabric is really a rich warm gold, not a colour cast), shot under near-neutral even light (~5200-5500K, close to neutral) on a pitch, real fabric weave and skin texture, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the edge of frame that ALREADY reads as a clean neutral grey, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, level.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The kit is genuinely warm gold and the frame was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/black-floor to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast / cool the warm cast' logic, or 'cools an imagined warm cast' chasing the gold kit, will push its neutral card off-neutral and strip the real product colour. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Level, do not straighten. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: portrait_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a fictional male footballer in a plain unbranded kit celebrating, on a pitch under mixed warm tunnel+floodlight, noticeably OVEREXPOSED and warm (blown-risk highlights on the shoulders and forehead), a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the frame edge, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, level.
inputs.realism_notes: Warm AND overexposed: the dominant move is to PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown areas, then cool the warm cast to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point -- opposite tonal AND WB direction from the cool daylight frames. Protect the recovered speculars. Level. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: portrait_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a fictional male footballer in a plain unbranded kit, shot under cold blue LED stadium light (~6500K, strong cool/blue cast), slightly dim, real texture, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the frame edge, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, level.
inputs.realism_notes: The coolest frame of the set -- strong blue LED cast, slightly dim, so it needs the LARGEST warm WB shift plus an exposure lift, still landing its grey card on the common white point. Its correction differs again from every other frame. Level. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: portrait_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal pitch-side sports portrait, raw unretouched look, a fictional male footballer in a plain unbranded dark kit with a bright, hot SCARLET-RED satin collar trim (vivid saturated red), on a night pitch under warm floodlights (~3300K warm cast), flat log-style colour, real satin sheen with folds and highlights on the collar trim, a small neutral 18% grey card clipped to the pitch-side board at the frame edge, documentary realism, no logos no flags no text, ~5200px long edge, 2:3 portrait, level.
inputs.realism_notes: The colourway-variant frame. Warm floodlit like the hero (its own WB/exposure decision to the shared look). The bright scarlet satin collar trim is the target for the masked in-family recolour: deepen it to a rich muted oxblood/burgundy (a within-red-family deepen-and-mute, well under a near-complementary rotation) riding the trim's own luminosity so the satin folds/sheen survive. The standard graded crop binds into this player's card; the burgundy variant is a SEPARATE deliverable. Level. Camera scale ~5200px.

inputs.name: crest_ref_1.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat vector-style artwork of a fictional football-tournament crest for the 'Continental Cup 2026': a clean shield/laurel emblem in two solid flat colours (deep navy and warm gold) on a plain flat white background, crisp hard edges, no gradients, no photographic texture, no drop shadow, generous white margin, centred, high resolution ~3000px. Abstract original emblem, NOT a copy of any real competition, club or national crest, no real flags, no text beyond the fictional wordmark 'CONTINENTAL CUP'.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE INPUT A -- the flat crest artwork that is the CORRECT source to vectorise. Flat solid two-colour art on white with a generous margin, so the honest path is prep-before-trace: crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock the white ground to transparency -> vectorise into a clean reusable SVG. Same 'kind of asset' by name as crest_ref_2 so the agent must decide which is traceable.

inputs.name: crest_ref_2.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal close-up product photograph of the SAME fictional 'Continental Cup 2026' crest rendered as an EMBROIDERED woven patch stitched onto dark textured jersey fabric, real raised thread stitching, fabric weave, soft folds and specular sheen catching studio light, shot on a light-grey studio sweep with a soft contact shadow, documentary product realism, no CGI, ~3200px, no extra text.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE DECOY -- looks like 'a second crest image' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of an embroidered patch on folded, textured fabric, so it CANNOT be traced into clean vector (thread weave, folds and sheen would become garbage paths). Its only correct use is the webshop product tile: knock the studio sweep to transparency with remove_background, then downscale/reframe. A naive agent that runs it through the same trace path used on crest_ref_1 produces an unusable SVG; the failure is only visible in the path data. Named same-kind as crest_ref_1 so the triage answer is not handed to the agent.

inputs.name: continental_card_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A3 (297x420mm) portrait player card -- ONE player per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<player_name>>, <<position>>, <<cap_no>>, <<tagline>>, <<tournament>>, plus TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a full-bleed player-photo frame bound to @Portrait (the graded portrait crop) and a masthead crest frame bound to @Crest (the vectorised tournament crest). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the crest reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: the merge emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW -- so a single-record A3 card is the correct connector-doable shape (a multi-up poster grid is impossible, a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind). Supplied as an input, never composed by the connector. TWO image columns (@Portrait, @Crest) mean the merge resolves the row's graded portrait AND the shared vectorised crest per card, giving the chain-produced crest a real connector-doable path onto every card without any free-form placement (AO-74/AO-75 two-image-column pattern).

inputs.name: continental_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns player_name,position,cap_no,tagline,tournament,@Portrait,@Crest holding EIGHT rows, one per featured player (fictional): Diego Solano, Marco Ferraz, Theo Rocher, Luka Petrov, Andre Mensah, Rafael Duarte, Nikolai Ivanic, Samuel Okoye. Each row carries a playing position (e.g. Forward, Winger, Midfielder), a squad/cap number (e.g. 10), a short poster tagline (e.g. 'Rise of a Nation'), and the tournament string 'Continental Cup 2026'. The @Portrait column names that player's finished graded portrait crop file; the @Crest column holds the SAME vectorised crest file (continental_crest.svg) in EVERY row so the merge drops the one shared masthead crest onto every card as a merge bind. Column names must exactly match the template fields <<player_name>>,<<position>>,<<cap_no>>,<<tagline>>,<<tournament>> and the two @image-path columns @Portrait and @Crest. Do NOT include any column that encodes how a portrait was lit or how it should be corrected, and do NOT reveal which crest source is traceable -- the CSV states card copy and file bindings only.
inputs.realism_notes: Card copy the merge binds verbatim; headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct portrait, AND the shared crest per card. @Crest carries the identical vectorised SVG path in all eight rows. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight cards. The CSV carries NO per-frame lighting/diagnosis and NO type/extension tell for the crest triage -- the treatment answer never sits in a field the agent is handed; the agent names the @Portrait crops per its own grade.

outputs.name: ContinentalCup_PlayerCards_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready A3 (297x420mm) portrait player cards -- ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) -- exported from the one-file-per-row page-layout data-merge; each card binds its player_name/position/cap_no/tagline/tournament verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralised graded portrait dropped into the full-bleed photo frame (via @Portrait) and the vectorised crest dropped into the masthead frame (via @Crest) -- both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. The featured hero (Diego Solano) is simply the FIRST page of this merged set, not a separately exported file.

outputs.name: graded_portraits_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralised portraits carried to one cinematic house look, delivered as the card-framed portrait crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralised masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralised master of each frame (the *_neutral output, its in-frame 18% grey card still present) -- the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point and one deep-but-unclipped black floor (no channel crushed to 0) while holding the warm-key cinematic look; and true-to-subject (no genuinely-coloured kit forced off); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered portrait crop (the *_card output that binds into that player's card) -- framed on the player with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame, which must be non-identical across the warm and cool frames.

outputs.name: hero_social_square.jpg
outputs.spec: Square 1:1 (~1440x1440) subject-aware crop of the graded, popped hero portrait for a square social post, same house grade, grey card out of frame, honest downscale from the ~5200px source (no upscale, no canvas extend), sRGB.

outputs.name: hero_social_vertical.jpg
outputs.spec: Vertical 9:16 (~1080x1920) crop of the graded, popped hero portrait for a vertical story format, same house grade, grey card out of frame, honest downscale from the ~5200px source (no upscale, no canvas extend), sRGB.

outputs.name: variant_okoye_trim_burgundy.jpg
outputs.spec: Colourway variant of Samuel Okoye's card portrait (portrait_08): the bright scarlet satin collar trim deepened to a rich muted oxblood/burgundy via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-red-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red -- an in-band adjacent shift, no near-complementary rotation) riding the trim's existing luminosity so its folds, sheen highlights and shadow stay natural, and nothing else in the frame (skin, kit, pitch) is touched -- no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.

outputs.name: continental_crest.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the tournament crest for the card masthead and wider kit, traced ONLY after the flat crest artwork is crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency -- razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground. Produced from the flat crest artwork (crest_ref_1), NOT from the photographed embroidered patch.

outputs.name: crest_patch_packshot.png
outputs.spec: Webshop product tile of the embroidered crest patch: the studio sweep knocked to transparency by image_remove_background and the subject reframed/downscaled to ~1600x1600, sRGB. A RASTER packshot with no vector paths -- this file proves the embroidered patch was correctly triaged as a photograph (routed to remove_background), not traced.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: portrait_01.jpg, portrait_02.jpg, portrait_03.jpg, portrait_04.jpg, portrait_05.jpg, portrait_06.jpg, portrait_07.jpg, portrait_08.jpg, crest_ref_1.png, crest_ref_2.png
connector_workflow.note: Single asset load: bring the eight pitch-side portraits and the two crest reference images into the working project so the grade, the vectorise and the triage can run against real asset references. Plumbing only -- not the difficulty. (The authored card template and roster are supplied data inputs consumed at the merge.)

HERO BRANCH (establishes the house target). Level the featured hero portrait before any grading or reframing so the later off-centre card/social crops are measured against a true horizon. Only the frames that are actually tilted are straightened; deciding which is part of the job.

Establish the studio's cinematic house look on the featured frame and record the settings as the target the rest of the set must hit: neutralise the in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE until it looks truly neutral (kill any cast), then build the high-contrast floodlit-at-night look from tone primitives -- set blacks deep but held off zero (never clipped), protect the floodlit highlight speculars, warm the key, add contrast/clarity, hold vibrance muted for a filmic palette. A reasoned authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. The agent never reads a pixel -- it dials by eye and REPORTS the temperature/tint/exposure/black values it chose; these define the common target. This *_neutral full-res frame (grey card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact.
Select the player subject on the graded hero to drive a selective lift. Semantic subject selection (allowed); returns a mask URI.

Masked selective edit: apply a small exposure/clarity/contrast lift to the player subject ONLY, using step 4's mask, so he carves off the dark stadium while the deep black floor set in step 3 is left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit -- not a whole-image push that would also lift the background and destroy the cinematic depth. Full-res popped hero retained for the card crop and both social crops.

Reframe the popped hero to the A3 card photo frame, framing on the player with the far-left grey card cropped OUT in the same move. Downscale/reframe of existing ~5200px pixels only -- canvas never grown, no pixels invented. This card crop (card removed) is what binds into the hero card; neutrality is graded on the retained hero_neutral master, never here.

Subject-aware 1:1 crop of the full-res popped hero to ~1440x1440 for the square social post, grey card outside the crop, same house grade. Honest downscale from the ~5200px source; never upscale or canvas-extend.

Subject-aware 9:16 crop of the full-res popped hero to ~1080x1920 for the vertical story format, grey card outside the crop, same house grade. Cut from the full-res popped hero (not from the already-cropped card) so the vertical target stays a pure downscale, no upscale.

Bring portrait_02 to the shared house look established on the hero: neutralise its own in-frame grey card BY EYE to the common white point and carry it to the same tonal target (deep unclipped black floor, warm key, muted filmic contrast), reasoning THIS frame's own white-balance and exposure rather than reusing the hero's numbers. REPORT the values applied. Retained *_neutral master (card in frame) is the neutrality artifact.
Crop the neutralised frame to the A3 card photo frame, framing on the player with the grey card cropped OUT. Downscale-only from the ~5200px source.
Level portrait_03 before grading (this frame is tilted; a different correcting angle than the hero).

Bring portrait_03 to the shared house look: neutralise its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the common white point and carry it to the same tonal target, reasoning its own white-balance and exposure. REPORT the values applied. Retained *_neutral master is the neutrality artifact.
Crop to the A3 card photo frame, player-framed, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Bring portrait_04 to the shared house look: neutralise its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the common white point and carry it to the same tonal target, reasoning its own white-balance and exposure. REPORT the values applied. Retained *_neutral master is the neutrality artifact.
Crop to the A3 card photo frame, player-framed, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Bring portrait_05 to the shared house look: judge its own in-frame grey card BY EYE and set white-balance so THAT card reads neutral, then match exposure and the shared black floor. Let this frame's own card drive the decision rather than the batch. REPORT the values applied (including if white-balance was held). Retained *_neutral master is the neutrality artifact.
Crop to the A3 card photo frame, player-framed, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Bring portrait_06 to the shared house look: recover its tonal range first, then neutralise its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the common white point and seat the shared black floor, reasoning its own white-balance and exposure. Protect the recovered highlights. REPORT the values applied. Retained *_neutral master is the neutrality artifact.
Crop to the A3 card photo frame, player-framed, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Bring portrait_07 to the shared house look: neutralise its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the common white point and carry it to the same tonal target, reasoning its own (largest) white-balance and exposure move. REPORT the values applied. Retained *_neutral master is the neutrality artifact.
Crop to the A3 card photo frame, player-framed, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Bring portrait_08 to the shared house look: neutralise its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the common white point and carry it to the same tonal target, reasoning its own white-balance and exposure. REPORT the values applied. This neutralised full-res frame feeds BOTH the standard card crop AND the collar-trim colourway branch, so keep it before cropping. Retained *_neutral master is the neutrality artifact.
Crop the neutralised frame to the A3 card photo frame (the standard scarlet-trim version that binds into this player's card), player-framed, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

On the graded full-res frame, semantically select only the satin collar trim ('the red satin collar trim on the kit'). Isolates the recolour to that part so skin, kit and pitch are untouched. Returns a mask URI -- a real object selection, not a hue or coordinate region.

Masked recolour pass 1 (consumes frame + trim mask): keep the trim in the red family but deepen it toward oxblood -- a small within-band hue nudge (well under a near-complementary rotation, staying in red/wine) together with a luminance drop that darkens the satin, letting the trim's existing luminosity carry the folds, sheen and shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolour path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint skin and kit) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the satin sheen) -- both are wrong here.

Masked recolour pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the collar lands on the rich muted oxblood/burgundy target instead of a still-bright candy red or a flat brick, still riding the original luminosity so the satin sheen and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.
Reframe the finished burgundy-trim variant to the same card/web frame as the set, grey card OUT. DELIVERABLE variant_okoye_trim_burgundy.jpg. Downscale-only from the ~5200px source.

CREST BRANCH -- prep-before-trace step 1 on the flat crest artwork: push contrast/clarity and drive the ground toward clean white so the two solid crest colours separate hard from the paper. A soft low-contrast source traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 2: crop away the generous margin to the tight bounds of the crest so the trace sees only the mark, not a field of white.
Prep-before-trace step 3: knock the white ground to transparency so the trace captures the crest shapes only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

Trace the prepared raster (crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the card masthead and wider kit. DELIVERABLE continental_crest.svg. Tracing the raw source, or the photographed embroidered patch, would produce a paper-bounded or fabric-weave garbage silhouette -- the prep-and-triage discipline this branch encodes.

Isolate the embroidered crest patch subject from its studio sweep for the webshop product tile: knock the sweep to transparency. This asset is a photograph of stitched fabric, so it is routed to a cut-out, not the tracer.

Subject-aware reframe + downscale of the patch cut-out to ~1600x1600 for the webshop tile, sRGB. DELIVERABLE crest_patch_packshot.png -- a raster with no vector paths. Pure downscale from the ~3200px source, never upscale or canvas-extend.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: portrait01_card, portrait02_card, portrait03_card, portrait04_card, portrait05_card, portrait06_card, portrait07_card, portrait08_card, continental_crest.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralised portrait crops plus the vector crest so the merge can resolve them by the @Portrait column (per-row player photo) and the @Crest column (the shared masthead crest).
